name: Operating Systems
description: Processes and threads, CPU scheduling, synchronisation, deadlock, memory management, virtual memory and file systems.

nodes.name: Kernel & system calls
nodes.desc: User and kernel mode, system calls, traps and interrupts as the way into the OS.
nodes.summary: You will understand how user programs enter the kernel through system calls, traps and interrupts and why dual-mode operation exists.
topics: System calls and the syscall interface

nodes.name: Processes
nodes.desc: The process abstraction, the PCB, multiprogramming and the parts of a process in memory.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe a process, its memory layout and its process control block, and explain how multiprogramming works.
topics: Process memory layout: text, data, heap, stack

nodes.name: Process states
nodes.desc: The process state diagram, context switches and what triggers each transition.
nodes.summary: You will be able to trace a process through the state diagram and identify the events that cause each transition and context switch.
topics: New, ready, running, waiting and terminated

nodes.name: fork and exec
nodes.desc: Process creation with fork, counting processes created by fork loops, exec and wait.
nodes.summary: You will be able to predict the processes created by fork calls, including in loops, and use exec and wait correctly.
topics: fork return values in parent and child
exec family replacing the process image

nodes.name: Threads
nodes.desc: Threads versus processes, what threads share, and user-level versus kernel-level threads.
nodes.summary: You will be able to contrast threads with processes, state what threads share and compare user-level and kernel-level threading.

nodes.name: CPU scheduling
nodes.desc: Scheduling criteria: turnaround, waiting and response time, throughput and CPU utilisation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define and compute the scheduling criteria used to compare CPU scheduling algorithms.

nodes.name: FCFS, SJF & SRTF
nodes.desc: Gantt charts for FCFS, SJF and SRTF and computing average waiting and turnaround times.
nodes.summary: You will be able to draw Gantt charts for FCFS, SJF and SRTF and compute average waiting and turnaround times from them.
topics: First-come first-served and the convoy effect

nodes.name: Round robin
nodes.desc: Round-robin scheduling, the time quantum and context-switch overhead.
nodes.summary: You will be able to schedule processes with round robin and analyse how the time quantum affects response time and overhead.

nodes.name: Priority scheduling
nodes.desc: Preemptive and non-preemptive priority scheduling, starvation and ageing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply preemptive and non-preemptive priority scheduling and prevent starvation with ageing.

nodes.name: Critical sections
nodes.desc: Race conditions and the critical-section problem: mutual exclusion, progress and bounded waiting.
nodes.summary: You will be able to identify race conditions and check whether a solution meets mutual exclusion, progress and bounded waiting.
topics: Mutual exclusion, progress and bounded waiting

nodes.name: Synchronisation
nodes.desc: Locks, hardware support (test-and-set, swap) and the synchronisation tools built on it.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build locks from hardware primitives like test-and-set and swap and reason about spinlocks and mutexes.

nodes.name: Semaphores
nodes.desc: Binary and counting semaphores, wait and signal, and tracing semaphore code.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use binary and counting semaphores with wait and signal and trace semaphore values through concurrent code.

nodes.name: Classic problems
nodes.desc: Producer–consumer, readers–writers, dining philosophers and barriers.
nodes.summary: You will be able to solve producer-consumer, readers-writers and dining philosophers problems with semaphores and recognise their pitfalls.

nodes.name: Precedence graphs
nodes.desc: Ordering concurrent statements with semaphores and parbegin/parend.
nodes.summary: You will be able to enforce an execution order on concurrent statements using precedence graphs, semaphores and parbegin/parend.

nodes.name: Deadlock
nodes.desc: The four Coffman conditions, resource allocation graphs and deadlock detection.
nodes.summary: You will be able to recognise deadlock using the four Coffman conditions and detect it with resource allocation and wait-for graphs.
topics: Cycles with single vs multiple instances

nodes.name: Banker's algorithm
nodes.desc: Safe states and safe sequences, and deadlock avoidance with the Banker's algorithm.
nodes.summary: You will be able to run the Banker's algorithm to find safe sequences and decide whether granting a request keeps the system safe.

nodes.name: Deadlock prevention
nodes.desc: Breaking a Coffman condition: resource ordering, preemption and wait-die / wound-wait.
nodes.summary: You will be able to prevent deadlock by breaking a Coffman condition using resource ordering, preemption or wait-die and wound-wait.
topics: Resource ordering to prevent circular wait

nodes.name: Contiguous allocation
nodes.desc: Fixed and variable partitions, first-fit, best-fit and worst-fit, internal and external fragmentation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to allocate memory with fixed and variable partitions and compare first-fit, best-fit and worst-fit placement.

nodes.name: Segmentation & linking
nodes.desc: Segment tables, relocation, overlays and dynamic linking of shared libraries.
nodes.summary: You will be able to translate segmented addresses with segment tables and explain relocation, overlays and dynamic linking.

nodes.name: Paging
nodes.desc: Pages and frames, page tables and translating a logical address to a physical one.
nodes.summary: You will be able to translate logical addresses to physical addresses using page tables, pages and frames.
topics: Splitting addresses into page number and offset

nodes.name: TLB & access time
nodes.desc: The translation lookaside buffer and the effective memory access time with TLB hits and misses.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute effective memory access time for a paged system with a TLB given hit ratios and access times.

nodes.name: Multilevel paging
nodes.desc: Page table size, page table entries and splitting the page table across levels.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute page table sizes and split addresses across levels of a multilevel page table.
topics: Page table entry size and contents

nodes.name: Virtual memory
nodes.desc: Demand paging, page faults and how a process can be larger than physical memory.
nodes.summary: You will understand how demand paging lets a process exceed physical memory and what happens during a page fault.

nodes.name: Page replacement
nodes.desc: FIFO, optimal and LRU replacement, counting page faults and Belady's anomaly.
nodes.summary: You will be able to count page faults for FIFO, optimal and LRU replacement and recognise Belady's anomaly.
topics: Counting page faults on reference strings

nodes.name: Working set
nodes.desc: Working sets, thrashing and the effective access time with page faults.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain thrashing, use the working set model to prevent it and compute access time with page faults.
topics: Effective access time with page faults

nodes.name: File systems
nodes.desc: Files, directories and the file-system interface, including Unix conventions.
nodes.summary: You will understand how files and directories are presented to programs and how Unix-style file systems organise them.

nodes.name: File allocation
nodes.desc: Contiguous, linked and indexed allocation, inodes and maximum file size, free-space management.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare contiguous, linked and indexed allocation and compute maximum file size for inode-based schemes.

nodes.name: Disk scheduling
nodes.desc: Disk geometry and access time; FCFS, SSTF, SCAN and LOOK disk scheduling.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute disk access time and total head movement for FCFS, SSTF, SCAN and LOOK scheduling.
topics: Disk geometry: platters, tracks and sectors
Seek time, rotational latency and transfer time
